clue.text: Footballers afford bills for mink at tremendous rate

parts.note: FA is the Football Association, the body governing English footballers
to stand someone a drink is to afford or pay for it
mink is a fur
IOUs are bills or promissory notes, so plural bills are IOUS

explanation.surface: Football players paying for mink coats with promissory notes at a startling pace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is only a link, and the bills come after the mink in the answer, though they come first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'fast and furious' describes action happening at a hectic, breakneck speed.

clue.text: Restoration not in question when making friends with zoo workers

indicators.note: making something of the given letters means building a new arrangement from them

parts.note: zookeepers are the workers who look after animals in a zoo

explanation.surface: Someone befriending the staff at the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is the anagram signal on 'friends'; 'when' and 'with' are links. The playground rule says whoever finds a thing may keep it.
explanation.definitionFit: The playground saying claims that whoever comes across a thing may keep it, so giving it back is out of the question.

clue.text: Barbarism of some, not all, including one five-year-old?

indicators.note: including means the shortened word holds the other pieces inside it
only part of the word some is used, its final letter being dropped

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
V is the Roman numeral for five
a year-old child is aged one, so aged stands for year-old

explanation.surface: Asking whether one five-year-old child counts as savage behaviour by some.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not all' drops the last letter of the word 'some', and 'including' wraps what is left round 'one five-year-old'. A year-old child is aged one.
explanation.definitionFit: Savagedom is the state or world of savages, an old word for barbarism.

clue.text: Fellow traders don't take a horse without right

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the horse wraps around the next piece

parts.note: gee, or gee-gee, is the nursery word for a horse, so a horse is A GEE

explanation.surface: Merchants refusing to accept a horse that comes without the proper title.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes the proverb 'Two of a trade never agree': people in the same business don't see eye to eye. 'take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This fills the gap in the old saying that rival tradesmen never concur, so the clue's phrase needs this verb.

clue.text: Take apart ideology, apart from the left, in a poet

indicators.note: in means the ideology is placed inside the poet's name
apart from says the letter for left goes in separately from the ideology, at another spot in the poet

parts.note: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy
L is the abbreviation for left
an ism is any doctrine or ideology

explanation.surface: Dismissing an ideology, with left-wing views excluded, as found in some poet's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart from' signals that the ideology and the left-hand letter go into the poet separately, at different places, and not as one block.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismantle a structure is to take it to pieces, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 1
Arm to cut when filming?

parts.note: a flick is a film, so filming suggests a flick
to knife something is to cut it with a blade

explanation.surface: A question about a limb being cut during a film shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arm' looks like the body part but means a weapon; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A switchblade with a blade that springs out is a weapon, and an arm is any weapon.

clue.text: Given fresh colour as requested by soldiers

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers; something done by them is the RE's, giving RES
to pray someone to do something is to request it earnestly

explanation.surface: Something painted anew at the soldiers' request.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'as requested by soldiers' as 'as the RE's prayed': the Royal Engineers (RE, a British army corps) in the possessive, then PRAYED. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A car that is resprayed has been painted again, getting a new colour.

clue.text: The root of topless dance

indicators.note: topless means the word's first letter is cut off

parts.note: the morris is a traditional English folk dance with bells and sticks

explanation.surface: The basic origin of dancing without a top on.
explanation.walkthrough: Morris dancing is an English folk dance performed by groups with bells on their legs. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is the fragrant root of certain irises, used in perfume.

clue.text: Believe it or not, good guy has scope for container of wine and herb

parts.note: ST, for saint, is the crossword's good person
range is scope, as in range of a gun
a butt is a large cask for wine or ale
rue is a bitter herb

explanation.surface: An amazing tale of a decent man with room for a cask of wine and some herbs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has', 'for' and 'and' are links joining the four pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock phrase introduces an amazing fact, just as 'believe it or not' does.

clue.text: Absolute refusal comes near to defining womankind

indicators.note: defining in its root sense of setting bounds means enclosing the next piece

parts.note: NR is the standard abbreviation for near, as in addresses
Eve, the first woman, stands for womankind

explanation.surface: A firm no drawing close to a definition of women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defining' is used in its root sense of 'setting limits round'. 'comes' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something will happen at no time at all is an emphatic refusal.

clue.text: "None my own work" is seen first in match recorder

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the recorder

parts.note: the scorer keeps the record at a cricket or football match

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of seen is used

explanation.surface: A plagiarist's confession spotted in a match scorer's book.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'scissors and paste', work put together by cutting up other people's writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A scissorer is a compiler who cuts out other people's material, so none of it is the compiler's own.

clue.text: A raptor or two could "show a leg" (wake) outside hospital

indicators.note: outside means the anagram goes round the next letter
show here works like 'cut a caper': the letters are made to perform in a new order

parts.note: H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Telling someone to get up and wake, while standing outside a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show a leg' is an old call to get up. A LEG WAKE, rearranged by 'show', goes round H. Two raptors because an eagle and a hawk are both in the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The eaglehawk is an Australian eagle, a bird of prey whose name joins two raptors.

clue.text: Be naughty again, by gum!

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
to sin is to do wrong, to be naughty

explanation.surface: An exclamation, 'by gum!', on misbehaving once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by gum!' is a northern English exclamation; 'by' is a link and 'gum' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is a sticky gum exuded by trees.

clue.text: Plant is all about past ending

indicators.note: about means the total goes round the next piece

parts.note: the sum is the total, all of it
-ed is the ending of a past tense verb

explanation.surface: A plant concerned only with the end of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedum is a genus of succulent plants, the stonecrops.

clue.text: Guy to escape — don't leave a thing

parts.note: a guy is a man
to get out is to escape

explanation.surface: A man running off, urged to take everything with him.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase means 'eat all': the pea is eaten pod and all. 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The French name of the sugar pea means 'eat everything', since nothing of the pod is left uneaten.

clue.text: Universal myth came about from internal problem

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around and reordered

parts.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A universal myth that arose from a problem inside.
explanation.walkthrough: U + MYTH + CAME rearranged by 'about'. 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stomach ache is quite literally a problem inside the body.

clue.text: Space in the West's for dualists

indicators.note: in means the space goes inside the next piece

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress, so the West's gives Mae's
a niche is a recess, a small space

explanation.surface: Room in the West for those who believe in two opposing powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the West' is Mae West, so 'the West's' is MAE'S, which holds NICHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Manichees followed Mani's doctrine of a cosmic struggle between light and darkness, the classic dualism.

clue.text: Towers of indigo in foreign fields

indicators.note: in means the dye goes inside the fields

parts.note: campi is Italian for fields
anil is the indigo plant and its dye

explanation.surface: Towers rising from indigo crops abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Campanili are Italian bell towers, the plural of campanile.

clue.text: Third international knockout number by doctor

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a number
an intern is a junior hospital doctor

explanation.surface: A boxing knockout scored by a doctor in a third international match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Comintern, or Komintern, was the Third International, the Soviet-led communist federation.

clue.text: See 1 down
Protest born from return to civvy street

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: A protest arising from someone going back to civilian life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link. Civvy street is British slang for civilian life.
explanation.definitionFit: Demob is release from the armed forces, sending a soldier back to civilian life.

clue.text: See 8
Delete, about as before

indicators.note: about means before goes round the next word

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Removing something, much as was done earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to wipe out, a direct synonym for delete.

clue.text: Final remark on something that's straight in the gold

indicators.note: in means the die goes inside the gold

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the idiom 'straight as a die' makes a die the thing that is straight

explanation.surface: A closing comment on something honest found in the gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is the French farewell, a parting word.

clue.text: Stimulation with acid to get process going

parts.note: kicks are thrills, as in 'for kicks'
tart means sour, acid

explanation.surface: Using acid as a stimulant to get things started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick-start something is to give it the push that sets it going.

clue.text: See 5 down
Singular cricketer resembling judge

indicators.note: singular means the plural-looking final letter is dropped

parts.note: Garry Sobers was the great West Indian all-rounder

explanation.surface: A lone cricketer who looks like a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke treats SOBERS as a plural and makes it singular. The definition plays on 'sober as a judge'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'sober as a judge' makes the word a likeness to a judge.

clue.text: To sum up, English boy is into food

indicators.note: into means the boy's pieces go inside the food

parts.note: pie is a food
Tom is a boy's name

explanation.surface: In short, an English lad is keen on eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To epitomise is to sum something up in brief.

clue.text: Dairy product, a small river going into a pipe

parts.note: Brie is a French cheese, a dairy product
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Cheese and a stream draining into a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going into' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A brier, or briar, is a tobacco pipe made from heath root.

clue.text: Maintenance in the cotton mill is a two-way affair

definitions.text: Maintenance in the cotton mill is a two-way affair

parts.words: Maintenance in the cotton mill is a two-way affair
parts.note: read literally, the upkeep of the looms' thread-carrying devices; also a transport link running back and forth

explanation.walkthrough: In a loom the shuttle carries the thread back and forth; servicing them is maintenance. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus or train running repeatedly between two places shuttles back and forth, two ways.

clue.text: See 27
